summary: Reddit, X and Bluesky were unreachable today, so every source here is a Hacker News comment from the last 7 days. The strongest threads were developers who don't trust coding agents with their keys, a fake-recruiter malware campaign that hides in take-home tests, and the collapse of cheap VPS stock. A few consumer gripes (Audible, the Syncthing Android app, Cloudflare's abuse form) round out the list.

ideas.title: Agent Key Recipes: least-privilege presets for AI coding agents
ideas.oneLiner: A local credential proxy for coding agents that ships ready-made allowlists per service (GitHub, Stripe, AWS, Supabase), so agents get a narrow slice of a key instead of a god-mode one.
ideas.problem: Secret-injection proxies keep the key out of the agent's context, but many services only issue all-powerful API keys, so the agent still has the full API surface. Tools that do filter requests need fiddly per-service rules that people aren't confident they got right.
ideas.targetUsers: Developers running Claude Code, Codex or similar agents on real accounts, and small teams that can't afford an agent wiping a production database.
ideas.monetization: Free local CLI with a few built-in recipes; paid Pro (about $8/month) for the full recipe library, a team-shared policy file and an approval-log dashboard.
mvp: Local HTTP proxy that swaps placeholder tokens for the real key from the OS keychain or 1Password
Recipe files: per-service allowlist of method, path and body fields, with GitHub, Stripe and Supabase presets
Dry-run mode that records what an agent tried and suggests a tighter recipe
Request log with one-tap allow or deny from phone or terminal
Works with any agent via a single base-URL or env var change

competitors.name: Docker Sandboxes (sbx secret)
competitors.gap: Injects secrets so the sandbox never sees them, but it doesn't narrow what the key can do, and commenters note it needs a Docker login and the secret loaded on the host.

competitors.name: nono
competitors.gap: Credential proxy plus kernel sandbox, but users report traffic that bypasses it (e.g. Tailscale nodes) and you write the profiles yourself.

competitors.name: Infisical Agent Vault
competitors.gap: One commenter says the company is end-of-lifing it and moving it to a hosted product.

competitors.name: KeyContain
competitors.gap: Fine-grained ACLs per service, but it is a hosted service the agent must opt into, and plain-English mapping per service is slow to build.

ideas.title: Preflight: scan a take-home or repo before you open it
ideas.oneLiner: Drop in a repo URL, zip or VS Code extension ID and get a plain-language report of anything that would run on open or install, before it touches your machine.
ideas.problem: Fake recruiters are sending developers take-home tests that execute code the moment the folder is opened or the dependency is installed, via VS Code extensions, tasks, install scripts or even instructions planted in agent files. People now assume all take-homes are hostile but have no quick way to check one.
ideas.targetUsers: Job-hunting developers, freelancers who receive client repos, and anyone who clones unfamiliar code and runs coding agents on it.
ideas.monetization: Free web scan for public repos; paid desktop or CLI app (about $5/month or $39 one-time) for local zips, private repos and a disposable-sandbox launcher.
mvp: Static scan for .vscode/tasks.json auto-run tasks, package.json install hooks, setup scripts and obfuscated blobs
Flags AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and README text that tells an agent to run commands silently
VS Code extension ID lookup showing publisher age, install count and permissions
Red / amber / green summary with the exact lines that triggered each flag
One-click open in a throwaway devcontainer

competitors.name: VS Code Workspace Trust and auto-task defaults
competitors.gap: Per a security write-up, newer VS Code versions turn off automatic tasks by default, but it relies on the user declining trust and doesn't cover install scripts, extensions or agent instructions.

competitors.name: Manual inspection guides
competitors.gap: Advice to read tasks.json and scripts yourself; no tool does it for you. My search found no dedicated pre-open scanner.

competitors.name: SIEM detection rules (e.g. SOC Prime)
competitors.gap: Aimed at security teams detecting the campaign after the fact, not at an individual developer checking a repo first.

ideas.title: A maintained Syncthing client for Android
ideas.oneLiner: A Flutter-fronted Android app that bundles Syncthing, is published on Play Store and F-Droid, and has a named maintainer.
ideas.problem: The official Syncthing Android app is discontinued, the popular fork was pulled from F-Droid, and users are scattered across unofficial forks and old APKs installed via adb for a tool they otherwise call low effort.
ideas.targetUsers: Privacy-minded Android users and self-hosters who sync photos, notes and password vaults between phone and desktop with Syncthing.
ideas.monetization: Free with a clear open-source core; optional paid supporter tier or one-time Pro unlock for scheduling, per-folder battery rules and a nicer status UI.
mvp: Embed the Syncthing core and manage it as a foreground service
Device and folder pairing by QR code
Battery, Wi-Fi-only and charging-only run conditions
Per-folder status and conflict list
Signed reproducible builds with a public release channel

competitors.name: Syncthing-Fork
competitors.gap: Was the main continuation, but in the thread a user reports it was pulled from F-Droid and the maintenance picture is unclear.

competitors.name: Official Syncthing Android app (discontinued)
competitors.gap: End of releases; a user still runs the end-of-line build via adb. Reported reason is Google Play's all-files-access policy, which also limits any new Play listing.

competitors.name: Termux or rclone workarounds
competitors.gap: Powerful but not friendly; a commenter falls back to rclone plus an FTP server on the phone.

ideas.title: Audible, minus the shop: library-only search and filters
ideas.oneLiner: A browser extension that makes audible.com search your own library by default, hides AI-narrated titles and warns when something you own has changed.
ideas.problem: Listeners say Audible's search pushes them toward the store, so they buy books they already own, and there is no way to filter out AI-narrated books. One reports paid-for books flipping to a buy-again button.
ideas.targetUsers: Heavy audiobook listeners with large libraries.
ideas.monetization: Free core; $12/year or $3 one-time for library snapshots, change alerts and wishlist cleanup.
mvp: Library-scoped search box injected into the Audible site
Owned badge on store results, with a warning before buying a book you already own
Toggle that hides AI-narrated titles
Local snapshot of your library with a diff when titles change
Bulk wishlist remove

competitors.name: Libation
competitors.gap: Desktop app for downloading and managing your Audible library; it doesn't fix site search or purchase mistakes, and users in my search describe it mainly as a DRM-removal tool.

competitors.name: OpenAudible
competitors.gap: Also a download manager; nothing found about owned-badges, AI-narration filters or change alerts.

competitors.name: Libro.fm
competitors.gap: A store alternative rather than a fix, and it means leaving an existing Audible library behind.

ideas.title: Abuse Router: report a scam site to the right place and track it
ideas.oneLiner: Paste a scam or impersonation URL and get every party that can act (host, CDN, registrar, search engines), a drafted report for each, and reminders to escalate.
ideas.problem: People trying to report sites that impersonate their company find Cloudflare's abuse form blank or unusable, and have no clear next step.
ideas.targetUsers: Small business owners, bloggers and security-minded individuals dealing with impersonation, phishing or copied sites.
ideas.monetization: Free for single reports; $9/month for evidence capture, tracking, escalation reminders and multi-site monitoring.
mvp: URL lookup of host, CDN, registrar and email provider with their abuse routes
Fallback path when a provider's form is broken (email address, escalation to upstream host)
Report drafts with auto-captured screenshots and archive links
Status tracker with 7-day follow-up reminders
Shareable evidence page

competitors.name: RrSG ACID Tool
competitors.gap: Identifies host, registrar and email provider with contacts, but it is a lookup only and points CDN-fronted sites back to the CDN.

competitors.name: Phish Report host identification
competitors.gap: Good provider identification and API, aimed at security teams; not a consumer workflow with tracking.

competitors.name: Manual WHOIS / RDAP lookups
competitors.gap: Records are often privacy-limited or point to upstream providers.

ideas.title: Cheap VPS stock and price watch with restock alerts
ideas.oneLiner: A tracker for sub-$15 VPS plans across providers, with in-stock status, price history and a ping when a plan comes back.
ideas.problem: Hobbyists say budget VPS plans are sold out and prices have doubled in months, and finding what is actually available means checking many sites. Some are giving up and buying used mini PCs to self-host.
ideas.targetUsers: Indie developers, students and hobbyists running small projects on cheap VPSs.
ideas.monetization: Free browsing; $3–5/month for restock alerts and price-drop notifications, plus affiliate links where providers allow them.
mvp: Scrapers or feeds for 10 to 15 budget providers
Filter by vCPU, RAM, disk, region and max price
In-stock status with last-checked time
Price history chart
Email or Telegram alert on restock or price drop

competitors.name: VPS Price Tracker
competitors.gap: Historical stock tracking, but centred on a single provider (RackNerd) per its own description.

competitors.name: ServerHunter
competitors.gap: Forum users say it can filter out-of-stock plans yet still lists many sold-out or non-working offers.

competitors.name: VPSBenchmarks
competitors.gap: Benchmark-focused, not a live stock or restock tool.

competitors.name: getdeploying.com
competitors.gap: Broad price comparison, no restock alerts.
